Read-only analysis in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Change nothing. Do not commit, push, or modify any file.

GOAL: Extract every reusable *lesson, pattern, and decision* from the SFCC-55 global footer work (branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, merged via PR #59). The output feeds a personal engineering playbook, so I want transferable knowledge, NOT a changelog.

Do this:

1. Identify the merge commit for PR #59 on `develop` and the full set of commits that came in with it. Use `git log`, `git show`, `gh pr view 59`, `gh pr diff 59`. Report the commit range you settled on and how you determined it.

2. For the footer subsystem, map what was actually built: every file under overrides/app/components/footer/ and any ui-kits component it depends on. For each, one line on its role. Note the atoms/molecules/organisms split and how theme recipes (`*.css.ts`) are wired via overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts.

3. Extract ESTABLISHED PATTERNS — things a future component should copy. Look specifically for:
   - the co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe pattern and how it's registered
   - how `var(--zimm-*)` tokens are used vs bare Chakra token keys
   - the container/presentational split (who fetches, who renders)
   - how region-scoping works (overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts) and why
   - how absent/failed CMS data is handled
   - the useUiCopy pattern for microcopy
   - test layering: what got a Vitest test, what got a Storybook play, and the stated reasoning

4. Read `gh pr view 59 --comments` in full. Extract every CodeRabbit finding that was DECLINED and the reasoning given in the reply. These declines encode real project conventions — capture the rule each one establishes, not just the finding.

5. Identify anything in the footer code that is a KNOWN COMPROMISE or deferred item — grep for TODO/FIXME/deferred/provisional/pending in the footer files, and note anything the PR conversation flagged as deliberately not fixed.

6. Note any place the footer code contradicts, or had to work around, the rules in .claude/rules/ or AGENTS.md.

Report as structured markdown. Quote real code with file:line. Prioritise things that would be non-obvious to someone building the NEXT component. Be explicit about what you could not determine.

########## hooks/useUiCopy.ts ##########
     1	import { createContext, useContext } from 'react';
     2	
     3	export type UiCopyContextValue = {
     4	  /**
     5	   * Returns the CMS value for `key`, or `fallback` while the fetch is loading, on fetch
     6	   * error, or when no `uiCopy` entry with that key exists yet.
     7	   */
     8	  t: (key: string, fallback: string) => string;
     9	  isLoading: boolean;
    10	};
    11	
    12	/**
    13	 * Populated by UiCopyProvider (overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider), mounted once in
    14	 * _app-config. Not meant to be consumed directly — call useUiCopy() instead, which supplies
    15	 * the no-Provider fallback.
    16	 */
    17	export const UiCopyContext = createContext<UiCopyContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
    18	
    19	const FALLBACK_ONLY: UiCopyContextValue = {
    20	  t: (_key: string, fallback: string) => fallback,
    21	  isLoading: false,
    22	};
    23	
    24	/**
    25	 * App-wide UI-copy lookup, backed by Contentful's uiCopy content type — one entry per string,
    26	 * fetched in a single bulk call by UiCopyProvider and shared via context, the same pattern
    27	 * this app already uses for translations (`useIntl`) rather than the per-page container-fetch
    28	 * pattern commerce-sdk-react hooks use. uiCopy is app-wide static content, not page-specific
    29	 * business data, so it's safe to call from any component — including presentational leaves —
    30	 * without threading it through as a prop.
    31	 *
    32	 * Safe to call with no UiCopyProvider mounted above it (Storybook, an isolated unit test):
    33	 * degrades to fallback-only text instead of throwing, so every call site stays functional and
    34	 * testable with zero setup.
    35	 *
    36	 * @returns `t` lookup function plus `isLoading`
    37	 */
    38	export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;

########## components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx ##########
     1	import React, { useCallback, useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react';
     2	import { useContentfulEntries } from 'app/hooks/useContentful';
     3	import { UiCopyContext } from 'app/hooks/useUiCopy';
     4	import type { UiCopyEntry } from 'app/types/contentful';
     5	
     6	type UiCopyProviderProps = {
     7	  children: ReactNode;
     8	};
     9	
    10	/**
    11	 * Bulk-fetches every `uiCopy` entry in one Delivery API call (`content_type=uiCopy`) and
    12	 * provides the resulting key→value lookup to every descendant via useUiCopy() — mounted once
    13	 * in _app-config, so creating N entries in Contentful costs one call for the whole app, not N
    14	 * calls from N components each independently fetching the same content.
    15	 *
    16	 * @param props.children the app tree to provide uiCopy lookups to
    17	 */
    18	export const UiCopyProvider = ({ children }: UiCopyProviderProps) => {
    19	  const { data, isLoading } = useContentfulEntries<UiCopyEntry>('uiCopy');
    20	
    21	  const copyMap = useMemo(() => {
    22	    const map = new Map<string, string>();
    23	    (data ?? []).forEach((entry) => {
    24	      map.set(entry.fields.key, entry.fields.value);
    25	    });
    26	    return map;
    27	  }, [data]);
    28	
    29	  // Fallback-on-failure by design, not just a loading placeholder: unlike structural content
    30	  // (e.g. FooterContainer's footerConfig, which renders nothing rather than substitute
    31	  // placeholder content), losing a button label or a status message to a Contentful outage
    32	  // should never blank a control.
    33	  const t = useCallback((key: string, fallback: string): string => copyMap.get(key) ?? fallback, [copyMap]);
    34	
    35	  const value = useMemo(() => ({ t, isLoading }), [t, isLoading]);
    36	
    37	  return <UiCopyContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</UiCopyContext.Provider>;
    38	};

########## utils/safeHref.ts ##########
     1	/**
     2	 * Allow-list guard for hrefs that originate outside the codebase.
     3	 *
     4	 * Anything reaching an `href` from Contentful, a URL parameter, or a prop supplied by a
     5	 * caller we do not control has to pass through here first. `javascript:` and `data:` URLs
     6	 * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
     7	 * lookahead rejects that, including the backslash form — a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`,
     8	 * so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as a second slash is. `e9c2180` closed
     9	 * only the forward-slash half; the backslash and control-character forms stayed open until now.
    10	 *
    11	 * Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a deny-list has to anticipate every scheme,
    12	 * and browsers keep adding them.
    13	 */
    14	// eslint-disable no-control-regex — the control characters ARE the subject here. The rule exists
    15	// to catch them appearing by accident; these are deliberate, and matching them is the whole point
    16	// of the fix. Suppressed at the point of use rather than in .eslintrc, per the escape-hatch
    17	// convention in .claude/rules/typescript.md.
    18	/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
    19	const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
    20	const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
    21	/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
    22	
    23	/**
    24	 * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
    25	 *
    26	 * The WHATWG parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
    27	 * in the input, BEFORE it parses. `/\u0009/evil.com` is therefore parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing
    28	 * the raw string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves — which
    29	 * is exactly how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open.
    30	 *
    31	 * A plain space is deliberately not stripped: the parser percent-encodes it rather than removing
    32	 * it, so `/ /evil.com` resolves on-site and must stay allowed.
    33	 */
    34	const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
    35	
    36	const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
    37	
    38	/** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
    39	export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false);

     1	import React, { useCallback, useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react';
     2	import { useContentfulEntries } from 'app/hooks/useContentful';
     3	import { UiCopyContext } from 'app/hooks/useUiCopy';
     4	import type { UiCopyEntry } from 'app/types/contentful';
     5	
     6	type UiCopyProviderProps = {
     7	  children: ReactNode;
     8	};
     9	
    10	/**
    11	 * Bulk-fetches every `uiCopy` entry in one Delivery API call (`content_type=uiCopy`) and
    12	 * provides the resulting key→value lookup to every descendant via useUiCopy() — mounted once
    13	 * in _app-config, so creating N entries in Contentful costs one call for the whole app, not N
    14	 * calls from N components each independently fetching the same content.
    15	 *
    16	 * @param props.children the app tree to provide uiCopy lookups to
    17	 */
    18	export const UiCopyProvider = ({ children }: UiCopyProviderProps) => {
    19	  const { data, isLoading } = useContentfulEntries<UiCopyEntry>('uiCopy');
    20	
    21	  const copyMap = useMemo(() => {
    22	    const map = new Map<string, string>();
    23	    (data ?? []).forEach((entry) => {
    24	      map.set(entry.fields.key, entry.fields.value);
    25	    });
    26	    return map;
    27	  }, [data]);
    28	
    29	  // Fallback-on-failure by design, not just a loading placeholder: unlike structural content
    30	  // (e.g. FooterContainer's footerConfig, which renders nothing rather than substitute
    31	  // placeholder content), losing a button label or a status message to a Contentful outage
    32	  // should never blank a control.
    33	  const t = useCallback((key: string, fallback: string): string => copyMap.get(key) ?? fallback, [copyMap]);
    34	
    35	  const value = useMemo(() => ({ t, isLoading }), [t, isLoading]);
    36	
    37	  return <UiCopyContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</UiCopyContext.Provider>;
    38	};

########## utils/safeHref.ts ##########
     1	/**
     2	 * Allow-list guard for hrefs that originate outside the codebase.
     3	 *
     4	 * Anything reaching an `href` from Contentful, a URL parameter, or a prop supplied by a
     5	 * caller we do not control has to pass through here first. `javascript:` and `data:` URLs
     6	 * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
     7	 * lookahead rejects that, including the backslash form — a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`,
     8	 * so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as a second slash is. `e9c2180` closed
     9	 * only the forward-slash half; the backslash and control-character forms stayed open until now.
    10	 *
    11	 * Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a deny-list has to anticipate every scheme,
    12	 * and browsers keep adding them.
    13	 */
    14	// eslint-disable no-control-regex — the control characters ARE the subject here. The rule exists
    15	// to catch them appearing by accident; these are deliberate, and matching them is the whole point
    16	// of the fix. Suppressed at the point of use rather than in .eslintrc, per the escape-hatch
    17	// convention in .claude/rules/typescript.md.
    18	/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
    19	const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
    20	const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
    21	/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
    22	
    23	/**
    24	 * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
    25	 *
    26	 * The WHATWG parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
    27	 * in the input, BEFORE it parses. `/\u0009/evil.com` is therefore parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing
    28	 * the raw string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves — which
    29	 * is exactly how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open.
    30	 *
    31	 * A plain space is deliberately not stripped: the parser percent-encodes it rather than removing
    32	 * it, so `/ /evil.com` resolves on-site and must stay allowed.
    33	 */
    34	const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
    35	
    36	const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
    37	
    38	/** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
    39	export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false);

     1	import React from 'react';
     2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
     3	import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';
     4	import { isSafeHref } from 'app/utils/safeHref';
     5	
     6	const ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE = 'ZimmContactIconRow';
     7	
     8	// Figma: Icon-list has pt-4px (alias/space/100) above it and 4px internal gap between icons.
     9	// hrefs are typically sourced from Contentful (FooterConfigEntry, HPC-034) by the caller. Until
    10	// that integration lands, absent hrefs render each icon as a non-interactive but labelled
    11	// <span> — visible in the layout and announced by screen readers, but absent from the tab
    12	// order. See the inline note on the fallback branch below for the full a11y reasoning. When a
    13	// href arrives it switches to a live <a>, no other changes needed.
    14	type ZimmContactIconRowProps = {
    15	  phoneHref?: string; // locale-aware tel: href
    16	  whatsAppHref?: string; // WhatsApp URL
    17	  emailHref?: string; // mailto: address
    18	};
    19	
    20	type ContactLink = { href?: string; label: string; icon: 'phone' | 'whatsapp' | 'email' };
    21	
    22	/**
    23	 * True when following the href would navigate away from the storefront.
    24	 *
    25	 * Takes `string | undefined` rather than `string` so the caller does not need an `as string` to
    26	 * satisfy it inside an isSafeHref branch. isSafeHref returns a plain boolean, which carries no
    27	 * narrowing, and a `href is string` predicate would be unsound — an unsafe value like
    28	 * `javascript:void(0)` is a string that returns false, so the else branch would narrow to
    29	 * `undefined` incorrectly. An absent href never leaves the site, so `?? ''` is the honest answer.
    30	 *
    31	 * Derived from the scheme rather than keyed to a channel name: tel: and mailto: hand off to the
    32	 * OS dialer or mail client and never navigate, so a target on them does nothing. An http(s)
    33	 * channel — WhatsApp today — is a real cross-origin navigation and opens in a new tab so a
    34	 * shopper mid-browse does not lose the site. Any future http(s) channel inherits this without
    35	 * another edit here.
    36	 */
    37	const leavesTheSite = (href: string | undefined): boolean => /^https?:/i.test(href ?? '');
    38	
    39	/** WCAG 3.2.5 — a link that opens a new tab has to say so in its accessible name. */
    40	const NEW_TAB_SUFFIX = ' — opens in a new tab';
    41	
    42	/**
    43	 * Contact channel icon row (phone / WhatsApp / email). Extracted from the footer so it can be
    44	 * reused anywhere a storefront needs the same channels — nothing here is footer-specific.
    45	 *
    46	 * @param props see ZimmContactIconRowProps
    47	 */
    48	export const ZimmContactIconRow = ({ phoneHref, whatsAppHref, emailHref }: ZimmContactIconRowProps) => {
    49	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CONTACT_ICON_ROW_RECIPE, {});
    50	  const links: ContactLink[] = [
    51	    { href: phoneHref, label: 'Call us', icon: 'phone' },
    52	    { href: whatsAppHref, label: 'WhatsApp', icon: 'whatsapp' },
    53	    { href: emailHref, label: 'Email us', icon: 'email' },
    54	  ];
    55	  return (
    56	    <chakra.div __css={styles.row}>
    57	      {links.map(({ href, label, icon }) =>
    58	        // isSafeHref, not a truthiness check: these typically arrive from Contentful, so a
    59	        // javascript:/data:/protocol-relative value would otherwise be rendered straight onto
    60	        // an anchor. Rejected values fall through to the span below, which is already the
    61	        // correct treatment for "no usable destination".
    62	        isSafeHref(href) ? (
    63	          <chakra.a
    64	            key={icon}
    65	            href={href}
    66	            // rel is explicit rather than relying on target="_blank" implying noopener: that is
    67	            // browser default behaviour, not a guarantee, and noreferrer also stops the
    68	            // storefront URL leaking to the third party.
    69	            {...(leavesTheSite(href) ? { target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener noreferrer' } : {})}
    70	            aria-label={leavesTheSite(href) ? `${label}${NEW_TAB_SUFFIX}` : label}
    71	            __css={styles.iconLink}
    72	          >
    73	            <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-hidden={true} />
    74	          </chakra.a>
    75	        ) : (
    76	          // Fallback for a channel with no usable destination — either the field is absent, or
    77	          // isSafeHref rejected the value. Both reach here, and both want the same treatment.
    78	          // NON-INTERACTIVE but PERCEIVABLE:
    79	          //   - <span>: no href, no tabIndex, so nothing promises an action that cannot be
    80	          //     performed (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance).
    81	          //   - labelled, not aria-hidden: ZimmIcon emits role="img" + aria-label, so screen
    82	          //     reader users learn the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoids the
    83	          //     1.1.1 information loss the previous aria-hidden caused).
    84	          // Not dead code: contact channels are optional per storefront, so a locale that
    85	          // supplies only e.g. email still renders the other two icons this way.
    86	          <chakra.span key={icon} __css={styles.iconLink}>
    87	            <ZimmIcon type={icon} size="md" aria-label={label} />
    88	          </chakra.span>
    89	        ),
    90	      )}
    91	    </chakra.div>
    92	  );
    93	};

10: *      through `theme.sizes`, not `theme.space`. The Zimmermann named scale is registered as
11: *      `space` only (deliberately — see foundation/sizes.ts), so `width: 'xl'` silently reads
12: *      Chakra's default `sizes.xl` = 36rem. It shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer.
14: *   2. The same trap on a typography property. `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are
15: *      deliberately NOT registered either (theme/index.ts explains why), so a bare key reads
16: *      Chakra's default or resolves to nothing at all. See TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS below.
18: *   3. A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe. `theme/index.ts` composes with
19: *      `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which DEEP MERGES — a recipe named `Footer` does
20: *      not replace SFCC's `Footer`, it inherits it. Shared part names then pick up base
21: *      properties, and a key you add that the base lacks is appended last, so a CSS shorthand
22: *      can silently reset a longhand the base declared earlier.

25: *      the entire value; `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim, the browser rejects the
26: *      declaration, and the padding does not apply at all.

═══════════════════════════════════════ 5ecd515
refactor(footer): decompose into atoms/molecules/organisms with co-located styles

What changed:
- Split footer/index.tsx (561 lines, 5 components in one file) into independently
  reusable pieces: ZimmModal (atom), ZimmContactIconRow (molecule),
  ZimmSubscribeSection/ZimmSubscribeModal (organisms), plus footer-local
  BottomBar/FooterNavColumn. footer/index.tsx is now pure assembly (~140 lines).
- Extracted the subscribe state machine into useSubscribeSection, and generalized
  useSubscribeModal -> useZimmModal so its focus/scroll/Tab-trap mechanics aren't
  form-specific. Both now have direct unit tests they lacked as inline logic.
- Co-located each component's theme recipe as <name>.css.ts beside it, replacing
  the single 506-line theme/components/footer.ts (6 recipes + a small
  footerShared.ts for the two values genuinely needed in more than one file).
  No runtime change: Chakra resolves a recipe by name, not file path.
- Fixed two accessibility bugs surfaced by local CodeRabbit review while touching
  this code: the bottom-bar locale control was a focusable, labelled button with
  no action (WCAG 3.2.4/4.1.2 — now a non-interactive div, same treatment as the
  contact-icon fallback); the modal's Tab trap couldn't recover focus once it
  landed outside the dialog (WCAG 2.1.2).
- Updated CODEOWNERS, protectedFiles.md, frozenFiles.md, and overrideStyling.md to
  match: ui-kits/ now has Tier 3 ownership (was previously uncovered by any rule),
  and co-located *.css.ts files route to squad review instead of the Tier 1/2
  UI-designer gate theme/components/ carries — documented as a deliberate,
  narrower exception, not a general loosening. Ran sync:ai-rules to regenerate
  the Cursor/Copilot mirrors of the changed rule docs.

Why: footer review feedback kept landing on "too much logic in one file, doesn't
follow our atom/molecule/organism structure." This establishes that pattern —
co-located styles, organism-level reuse — as the example other component
overrides should follow.

═══════════════════════════════════════ 9d5f89c
refactor(theme): require var(--zimm-*) over bare Chakra token keys in overrides

What changed:
- Replaced 24 bare spacing-scale keys (gap/padding*/margin*, e.g. 'xs', '2xs',
  '3xl') and 5 bare semantic colour tokens ('background.05', 'text.inverse',
  etc.) with their var(--zimm-*) equivalents, across 9 files. Both forms
  resolve to the identical value (theme.space/theme.colors ARE registered from
  the Zimmermann foundations — see theme/index.ts) — this is a house-style
  change, not a bug fix. Two of the instances were in JSX (footerNavColumn's
  sx merge), not just recipe files.
- Caught mid-fix: zimmTextInput.css.ts's `top: floated ? '3xs' : '50%'` had a
  bare key hiding inside a conditional branch. Fixed, and fixed the guard that
  should have caught it (see below) — the component's own test asserted the
  old bare value and needed updating too.
- Extended theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts with a new guard: no
  override-component style may use a bare token key on a registered scale.
  Runs on every `npm run test`, so this becomes a mechanical PR check rather
  than something a reviewer re-verifies by eye each time.
- That new guard initially had the same blind spot as the bug it was built to
  catch: it resolved a function-form baseStyle (zimmTextInput's) with a single
  fixed all-false props object, so a value that only appears down a
  conditional branch — like the '3xs' above — was never walked. Fixed by
  resolving across all 2^n combinations of the function's boolean props
  instead of one. Verified this actually works by reintroducing the bare
  '3xs' and confirming the guard fails on it, then restoring the fix.

  ZimmSubscribeSection rendered its unavailable/error failure copy with the
  same `success` style as the success message — a shopper saw failure text
  styled as a confirmation. Added a dedicated `error` part (inverse-mode
  error colour, matching the pattern zimmTextInput.css.ts's error state
  already uses) and role="alert" on the failure message.
- Updated overrideStyling.md (hierarchy point 2) and css.md (token example)
  to document var(--zimm-*) as required, not just preferred, and to point at
  the new mechanical guard.

Why: bare Chakra token keys and var(--zimm-*) both resolve correctly today,
but a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check theme/index.ts's registered-scale
list to know whether it's actually correct — a raw zimm var is unambiguous at
every call site regardless.

previous commit, which only worked because FooterContainer was the sole
consumer. Context sharing removes the redundant-fetch concern that motivated
that pattern in the first place.

Cleaned up BottomBar and ZimmSubscribeSection to match: both dropped their
copyrightLabel/emailLabel/subscribeButtonLabel/successMessage/
unavailableMessage props entirely and call useUiCopy() directly instead.
Footer/FooterContainer shed all the prop-threading that existed only to plumb
these through — footer/index.tsx is back to being purely about footerConfig.

Tests migrated to match, not just patched:
- useUiCopy.test.tsx (renamed from .ts, now has JSX): context passthrough +
  no-Provider fallback, 2 tests.
- uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx (new): the 5 fetch/map-building tests that
  used to live in useUiCopy.test.ts.
- zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx: the 2 prop-override tests became
  useUiCopy-mock-based tests.
- footer/index.test.tsx: removed the now-inapplicable useUiCopy mock and
  wiring test.

252/252 tests pass, tsc/eslint clean.

refactor(footer): descope the HPC-035 name-capture modal behind an opt-in prop

SFCC-55's AC scopes the Stay in Touch section to "an email input field and submit button as a
placeholder component", and the story defers the Omneo sign-up and states the footer is built
"without any content behind the different links and buttons". A modal collecting names to POST
to Omneo is content behind a button.

The modal itself is a real requirement — HPC-035 and HPC-037, both confirmed in
.docs/prd/homepage.md §6 — but it belongs to that flow, not to this story's AC, and it has no
design: all nine of its theme parts carry no Figma node reference, against 27 Figma-referenced
parts elsewhere in footer.ts. Shipping it would put undesigned UI on eight storefronts and give
QA a layout the designer never signed off; the 2 July note on the story records Dani's design
sign-off as still pending.

So enableNameCapture defaults to false and the modal is not mounted. Submitting a valid email
resolves straight to the placeholder message, which is what the AC describes. The email is
cleared from the pending-signup ref on that path — nothing was sent, so nothing needs retaining.

The modal code and its coverage are kept and still exercised by two stories that opt in, so
HPC-035 inherits working, tested code rather than a rebuild. A new SubscribePlaceholder story
covers the path that actually ships. Mutation-tested: defaulting the prop back to true fails it.

═══════════════════════════════════════ 7e8f3cc
fix(utils): make region tie-break independent of Contentful response order

pickMostSpecificByRegion resolved ties by most-recently-updated, but the warn and
the reassignment both sat inside `if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt)`. Two
consequences, both silent:

- Equal or absent timestamps failed the strict `>`, so nothing fired and
  whichever entry the CDA happened to return first won. getEntries is called
  with no `order`, so that is not stable across requests.
- A tie already arriving newest-first never warned, defeating the documented
  purpose of surfacing the duplicate entry for cleanup.

The warn now sits outside the comparison, so it fires on every tie whichever side
wins, and `sys.id` breaks a dead heat as a secondary key. Verified stable across
every permutation of six candidate shapes.

The suite was testing around the bug. `test('order of the tied candidates in the
input does not change the outcome')` used only *distinct* timestamps — the one
arrangement that was already order-independent — and omitted the warn assertion
that would have caught the nesting. Renamed to say what it covers, plus five new
cases: identical timestamps, absent timestamps, a losing-candidate tie (the only
order that distinguishes "warns on every tie" from "warns when the candidate
wins"), a newer-timestamp-vs-lower-sys.id case pinning `sys.id` as *secondary*,
and an unscoped tie.

Mutation-tested rather than assumed. Un-hoisting the warn now fails 4 tests
(1 before these additions); promoting sys.id to primary fails 1; the pre-fix code
fails 4. Every new assertion was confirmed to die under at least one mutation.

Also corrected two untruths in the surrounding prose: the JSDoc said ties were
between "non-global" entries, but two unscoped entries tie at Infinity and do
warn; and the runtime message still promised "most-recently-updated" when sys.id
may decide it.

Warns n-1 times for an n-way tie, once per mount (the call sits in a useEffect
keyed on [client, site.id], not on every render) and is ungated by NODE_ENV, so
it does reach shopper consoles.

═══════════════════════════════════════ 9ec0740
fix(footer): reserve the subscribe control slot so the result message cannot shift the layout

Submitting an email grew the footer 490 → 512. The field and the message are built differently —
the form is 45px (36px content + 4/4 padding + 1px border) while the message was 68px (36px of
wrapped body2 plus its own 16/16 padding) — and nothing reserved the slot, so the 23px difference
propagated: slot 45 → 68, subscribe column 163 → 186, footer +22.

Figma's success state (node 4019:46044) keeps a Textfield instance at 320x59 at the same y=82 and
the footer stays 476 in both states: the message is a state of the field, occupying the field's
box, not a paragraph with padding of its own. So the slot is now reserved and the message no
longer supplies vertical padding.

Both halves are load-bearing, which the measurements only showed at mobile. Dropping the padding
alone appears to fix it at desktop and tablet — the message becomes shorter than the field, so the
column shrinks 9px and the taller site-map column keeps the row height unchanged. On mobile the
columns stack and the footer moves. Verified Δ0 on footer, content row, column and slot at 1440,
768, 375 and 320, with no clipping or text overflow.

minHeight rather than height so copy needing a third line grows instead of clipping; the centring
only positions the message and does not define its height, so its textStyle leading is intact.

SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT is 45px measured from our own render, not a design value — Figma specifies 59
and there is no token for it (actionSizes.height offers 52 and 40). Annotated as provisional with
the node reference, pending Kiera; adopting 59 would also grow the idle state by 14px.

SubscribePlaceholder now asserts no shift on both the slot and the footer. The slot assertion is
what makes it work: a footer-only check passes under both regressions at Storybook's viewport,
for the same reason the desktop measurement was misleading. Mutation-tested against a rebuilt
Storybook — removing the reservation and restoring the padding each fail it.

now trivially importable from any component, anywhere, the same way useIntl()
already is in this app: no Storybook/test setup required, since useUiCopy()
degrades to fallback-only text with no Provider mounted rather than throwing.

This replaces the footer-only container-fetch-and-prop-drill pattern from the
previous commit, which only worked because FooterContainer was the sole
consumer. Context sharing removes the redundant-fetch concern that motivated
that pattern in the first place.

copyrightLabel/emailLabel/subscribeButtonLabel/successMessage/
unavailableMessage props entirely and call useUiCopy() directly instead.

resolves straight to the placeholder message, which is what the AC describes. The email is

═══════════════════════════════════════ 7e8f3cc
fix(utils): make region tie-break independent of Contentful response order

pickMostSpecificByRegion resolved ties by most-recently-updated, but the warn and
the reassignment both sat inside `if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt)`. Two
consequences, both silent:

- Equal or absent timestamps failed the strict `>`, so nothing fired and
  whichever entry the CDA happened to return first won. getEntries is called
  with no `order`, so that is not stable across requests.
- A tie already arriving newest-first never warned, defeating the documented
  purpose of surfacing the duplicate entry for cleanup.

The warn now sits outside the comparison, so it fires on every tie whichever side
wins, and `sys.id` breaks a dead heat as a secondary key. Verified stable across
every permutation of six candidate shapes.

The suite was testing around the bug. `test('order of the tied candidates in the
input does not change the outcome')` used only *distinct* timestamps — the one
arrangement that was already order-independent — and omitted the warn assertion
that would have caught the nesting. Renamed to say what it covers, plus five new
cases: identical timestamps, absent timestamps, a losing-candidate tie (the only
order that distinguishes "warns on every tie" from "warns when the candidate
wins"), a newer-timestamp-vs-lower-sys.id case pinning `sys.id` as *secondary*,
and an unscoped tie.

Mutation-tested rather than assumed. Un-hoisting the warn now fails 4 tests
(1 before these additions); promoting sys.id to primary fails 1; the pre-fix code
fails 4. Every new assertion was confirmed to die under at least one mutation.

Also corrected two untruths in the surrounding prose: the JSDoc said ties were
between "non-global" entries, but two unscoped entries tie at Infinity and do
warn; and the runtime message still promised "most-recently-updated" when sys.id
may decide it.

Warns n-1 times for an n-way tie, once per mount (the call sits in a useEffect
keyed on [client, site.id], not on every render) and is ungated by NODE_ENV, so
it does reach shopper consoles.

═══════════════════════════════════════ 9ec0740
fix(footer): reserve the subscribe control slot so the result message cannot shift the layout

Submitting an email grew the footer 490 → 512. The field and the message are built differently —
the form is 45px (36px content + 4/4 padding + 1px border) while the message was 68px (36px of
wrapped body2 plus its own 16/16 padding) — and nothing reserved the slot, so the 23px difference
propagated: slot 45 → 68, subscribe column 163 → 186, footer +22.

Figma's success state (node 4019:46044) keeps a Textfield instance at 320x59 at the same y=82 and
the footer stays 476 in both states: the message is a state of the field, occupying the field's
box, not a paragraph with padding of its own. So the slot is now reserved and the message no
longer supplies vertical padding.

Both halves are load-bearing, which the measurements only showed at mobile. Dropping the padding
alone appears to fix it at desktop and tablet — the message becomes shorter than the field, so the
column shrinks 9px and the taller site-map column keeps the row height unchanged. On mobile the
columns stack and the footer moves. Verified Δ0 on footer, content row, column and slot at 1440,
768, 375 and 320, with no clipping or text overflow.

minHeight rather than height so copy needing a third line grows instead of clipping; the centring
only positions the message and does not define its height, so its textStyle leading is intact.

SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT is 45px measured from our own render, not a design value — Figma specifies 59
and there is no token for it (actionSizes.height offers 52 and 40). Annotated as provisional with
the node reference, pending Kiera; adopting 59 would also grow the idle state by 14px.

SubscribePlaceholder now asserts no shift on both the slot and the footer. The slot assertion is
what makes it work: a footer-only check passes under both regressions at Storybook's viewport,
for the same reason the desktop measurement was misleading. Mutation-tested against a rebuilt
Storybook — removing the reservation and restoring the padding each fail it.

@@ -2,6 +2,23 @@
 
 Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.
 
+**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
+covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
+decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
+renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
+Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
+**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
+elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
+right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
+component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
+component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
+and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
+`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
+resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
+render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
+(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
+below for single-parent internal components still applies there.
+
 | Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
 |---|---|---|---|---|
 | Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
@@ -55,6 +72,17 @@ Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
 - **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
 - **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
 - Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
+- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
+  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
+  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
+  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
+  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
+  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
+  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,

+2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
+   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
+   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
+   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
+   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
+   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
+   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
+   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
+   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
+   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
+   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
+   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
+3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
+   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
+   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
+   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
+   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
+   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
+   type" below.
+instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
+sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
+before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
+`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
+(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
+from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
+contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
+the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
+existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
+2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
+full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
+genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
+Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
+mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
+Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
+which is what `audit:tokens` is for.
+  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
+Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
+either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
+beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
+with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
+`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
+— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
+`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
+form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
+used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
+`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
+so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.
+
+See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
+`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
+traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
+Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
+recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
+SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
+numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)
+
+**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
+co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:
+
+```ts
+[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
+```
+
+The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
+recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
+responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
+`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.
+`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
+`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
+overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme
+recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second
+export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.
+
+**As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all** — no component override, no
+theme recipe, nothing registered for them in `theme/components/index.ts`. Verify current
+state before relying on any of this. `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS` list those
+paths forward-lookingly, not descriptively. An earlier revision of this paragraph cited
+`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as holding their styling; neither
+file has ever existed on any branch.
+## Co-locating a component's theme file
+
+A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
+`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, or an organism's own
+`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts`) instead of in
+`theme/components/`. Either way it's still registered in
+`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key
+passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an
+organisational choice with no runtime difference.
+
+**Governance follows the file, not the folder.** `theme/components/` is Tier 2, gated to
+the UI designer (protectedFiles.md). A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is deliberately routed
+differently: CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule sends it to the
+owning squad(s) only, dropping the Tier 1/2 approver requirement that the surrounding
+directory (e.g. `header/`, `footer/`) otherwise carries. That's intentional — a co-located
+file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
+(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
+actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
+recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
+files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.
+
+> **Known inconsistency, flagged not resolved.** This paragraph used to cite `button.ts`'s
+> `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` as the designer-gated example. That file
+> is now `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`, which the `**/*.css.ts` rule above
+> routes to the squads — so those provisional, unapproved constants are **no longer
+> designer-gated**, while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. The example was swapped
+> to `header.ts` (genuinely still gated) so this paragraph stops asserting something false.
+> Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc
+> fix, and is deliberately left open here.
+
+**Enforcement gap, partially closed:** the Tier 1/2 human reviewer was, until this rule
+existed, the only thing catching a hardcoded hex/px/rem/em value landing in a theme file.
+`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, see the `Never` note above) now exists
+and runs correctly against the real codebase — built 2026-08-23. What's still open: it is not
+wired into CI, so it only catches something if a developer or reviewer remembers to run it —
+removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic*
+backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI
+check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an
+optional nice-to-have — and per the script's own header, someone should triage a full run's
+findings first (14 pre-existing, unrelated violations turned up the day it was built) before

=== auditTokenUsage.mjs header (1-45) ===
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Token usage audit — flags a raw hex colour / px / rem / em literal in an override component
 * or theme recipe, where a Zimmermann token (a foundation constant, a var(--zimm-*) reference,
 * or a Chakra prop resolving through a registered scale) should be used instead.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
 *
 * Scope: overrides/app/components/** and overrides/app/theme/components/** — .ts/.tsx/.scss.
 * Deliberately excludes:
 *   - overrides/app/theme/foundation/ — not under either scan root; these files ARE the source
 *     of truth, so a raw value there is the point, not a violation.
 *   - *.test.ts(x) and *.stories.tsx — test assertions and Storybook demo code routinely need
 *     illustrative/representative raw values that aren't "a hardcoded design value shipped to
 *     production" in the sense this audit cares about (testing.md already treats these
 *     differently from production styling rigor).
 *
 * A match is downgraded from a failure to an ACKNOWLEDGED exception (still printed, does not
 * affect the exit code) when the contiguous non-blank block of lines ending at the match — i.e.
 * the match's own line plus every line above it up to the nearest blank line or file start —
 * contains "provisional", "pending", "placeholder", or an explicit "audit-allow". This is the
 * exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for every documented raw-value exception today
 * (e.g. zimmButton.css.ts's BTN_HEIGHT_LG/BTN_HEIGHT_SM/BTN_PADDING_Y, footer.css.ts's
 * SPACE_SECTION/SIZE_COL_SUB/SIZE_COL_MAP). Reading the existing explanatory comment as the
 * allow-list entry avoids a second, separately-maintained list that would drift from the code
 * the moment either one changes.
 *
 * The "nearest blank line" boundary, not a fixed line count, matters: this codebase's real
 * exception comments are often a shared multi-line block covering several sibling declarations
 * (footer.css.ts's four provisional constants share one comment), or wrap the marker word
 * itself across a line break (zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts had "...52/40. Pending\n// Kiera."
 * — "Pending" and "Kiera" on different lines). A fixed N-line window missed both shapes during
 * this script's own first calibration pass against the real codebase.
 *
 * This is a line-based grep, not an AST parse — matches
 * .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's own framing ("it greps for exactly this"). A real
 * false-positive class this cannot fully rule out: a hex-looking string in a non-colour
 * context (e.g. a URL fragment that happens to be 3-8 hex characters) would still be flagged;
 * mark it with `// audit-allow: <reason>` rather than trying to make the regex smarter.
 *
 * Not wired into CI yet — see overrideStyling.md's note on why (someone needs to own triaging
 * false positives on a real run first).
 */

########## zimmModal atom index.tsx ##########
     1	import React from 'react';
     2	import { createPortal } from 'react-dom';
     3	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
     4	
     5	const ZIMM_MODAL_RECIPE = 'ZimmModal';
     6	
     7	type ZimmModalProps = {
     8	  /** Whether the dialog is open. Nothing renders until this and `mounted` are both true. */
     9	  isOpen: boolean;
    10	  /** From the paired useZimmModal() call — false until the first client render, so the portal
    11	   *  is never created during SSR. */
    12	  mounted: boolean;
    13	  /** Called on backdrop click (and on Escape, via useZimmModal's own keydown listener). */
    14	  onClose: () => void;
    15	  /** Dialog panel max-width. No default — each modal type has its own Figma-specified size, so
    16	   *  a caller-supplied value is safer than a guessed generic default. */
    17	  maxWidth: string;
    18	  /** id of the element that labels the dialog (aria-labelledby). */
    19	  labelledBy: string;
    20	  /** id of the element that describes the dialog (aria-describedby), if one exists. */
    21	  describedBy?: string;
    22	  children: React.ReactNode;
    23	};
    24	
    25	/**
    26	 * Generic modal chrome — portal, backdrop, and an accessible dialog panel. Owns none of the
    27	 * content: a caller supplies its own form/fields as children and pairs this with useZimmModal()
    28	 * for focus/scroll/keyboard mechanics. Split out of the footer's original SubscribeModal so any
    29	 * future dialog — not just the subscribe flow — can reuse the same accessible shell.
    30	 *
    31	 * @param props see ZimmModalProps
    32	 */
    33	export const ZimmModal = ({
    34	  isOpen,
    35	  mounted,
    36	  onClose,
    37	  maxWidth,
    38	  labelledBy,
    39	  describedBy,
    40	  children,
    41	}: ZimmModalProps) => {
    42	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_MODAL_RECIPE, {});
    43	
    44	  const handleBackdropClick = (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    45	    if (e.target === e.currentTarget) onClose();
    46	  };
    47	
    48	  if (!mounted || !isOpen) return null;
    49	
    50	  return createPortal(
    51	    <chakra.div role="presentation" onClick={handleBackdropClick} __css={styles.overlay}>
    52	      <chakra.div
    53	        role="dialog"
    54	        aria-modal="true"
    55	        aria-labelledby={labelledBy}
    56	        aria-describedby={describedBy}
    57	        __css={{ ...styles.panel, maxWidth }}
    58	      >
    59	        {children}
    60	      </chakra.div>
    61	    </chakra.div>,
    62	    document.body,
    63	  );
    64	};

=== protectedFiles.md diff (additions) ===
+overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/
+`uiCopyProvider/` is mounted once inside `_app-config` and provides `useUiCopy()`'s context
+value to every page on every site — the same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, so it
+belongs in this tier alongside it rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission.
+
+A component's own recipe may instead live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
+`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`) rather than here — see
+[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s co-location pattern, introduced with the
+footer decomposition. It's still registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`
+either way. A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is **not** governed by this section's Tier 2
+UI-designer gate — CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule routes it to
+the owning squad(s) only. This folder's Tier 2 designation still applies to whatever
+hasn't moved to co-location, and to genuinely cross-component shared values (e.g.
+`footerShared.ts`) that a single component's file can't own.
+
+These files define the Zimmermann content model, authored once as a single
+organization-scoped Contentful **Environment Template** (`npm run sync:contentful`,
+via `client.environmentTemplate.*` in the `contentful-management` SDK) and installed
+into each environment (`npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>`). This replaced
+an earlier per-environment `sync.js` + migration-file pipeline once Contentful moved to
+recommending organization-level content models over independently-synced
+space/environment content types.
+
+`content-types/*.js` is the sole source of truth per content type (including
+`localized`/`required`/`validations` — there is no longer a separate migration file that
+overrides an inferior default). Field deletion during an install is opt-in
+(`--delete-deleted-fields`), off by default — a mistaken field definition pushed to the
+production Contentful environment is difficult to undo and may break running components.
+scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js
+scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs
+Always run `install:contentful` against a non-production Contentful environment first.
+Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` and `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (local / CI only —
+never deployed to MRT).

=== frozenFiles.md diff (additions) ===
-**No font binaries in this repo.** Futura Round ships under a Monotype *"Font Software For
-Desktop End User License Agreement"* which forbids "further distribute the Font Software, or
-any copy thereof" and "Install the Font Software on any server or in any digital asset
-management system" — so `.woff2`/`.otf` must not be committed here or served from the MRT CDN.
-Licence: Zimmermann-Handover repo, `02-design/library/assets/Font Futura WOFF2/Licenses/2275/`.
-Type renders from the fallback stack in `foundation/fonts.ts`. Self-hosting needs Zimmermann's
-own Monotype Web Page Content entitlement (2 fonts: Regular 400, Medium 500).
-
-Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` and are
-**Tier 2** — see [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
+**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
+Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
+`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
+`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
+resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.
+
+There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
+revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
+`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
+`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
+published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.
+
+`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
+declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
+The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
+design-parity review against Figma.
+
+Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
+the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
+component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see
+[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`

content.content:
# Description

Builds the global footer per SFCC-55 — shell, layout, and component structure across
all eight storefronts and both breakpoints. Content is Contentful-shaped but
fixture-backed: the CMS integration, link destinations, and Omneo sign-up are
separate stories, so `FooterContainer` supplies `FOOTER_FIXTURE` and `Footer` itself
takes its content as a required prop and fetches nothing.

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are

=== architecture.md additions ===
+- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing, sizes, motion, and the `--zimm-*` registry in `zimmTokens.ts` — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); the `.zimm-*` global classes composed from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2); a per-component override lives either one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2, UI-designer gated) **or**, per the co-location pattern, beside its component as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g. `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` — governed by that component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead). Either way it's registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. See [.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md](../.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md) > Co-locating a component's theme file. Note: brand fonts (Futura Round) **are** self-hosted — two faces ship from `overrides/app/static/fonts/` via `theme/fontFace.tsx`, mounted unconditionally, so they are served on every tier. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md) > Design System.
+Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are
+authored in code as one organization-scoped **Environment Template** and installed into
+each environment — Contentful's current recommended mechanism, replacing an earlier
+per-environment sync pipeline. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and
+team-safe.
+- `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` — assembles every content type in the definitions directory into one `EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`
+- `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — validates then installs the template's current version into one target environment
+- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `footerConfig.js`), the sole source of truth for its fields (including `localized`/`required`/`validations`)
+3. Run `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` for each environment in the promotion chain
+**To run it:**
+npm run install:contentful -- --target dev
+Requires `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (scope:shared) and `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account (scope:personal, never pushed to the centrally-shared GitHub Environments store, but fine to hold locally). Both live in your local, gitignored `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold them, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running). Get the management token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.
+Both scripts are idempotent — safe to re-run. Field deletion during an install is opt-in
+(`--delete-deleted-fields` on `install:contentful`), off by default.
+**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding content-type entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

Either way it's registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. See [.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md](../.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md) > Co-locating a component's theme file. Note: brand fonts (Futura Round) **are** self-hosted — two faces ship from `overrides/app/static/fonts/` via `theme/fontFace.tsx`, mounted unconditionally, so they are served on every tier. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md) > Design System.
+Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are
+authored in code as one organization-scoped **Environment Template** and installed into
+each environment — Contentful's current recommended mechanism, replacing an earlier
+per-environment sync pipeline. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and
+team-safe.
+- `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` — assembles every content type in the definitions directory into one `EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`
+- `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — validates then installs the template's current version into one target environment
+- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `footerConfig.js`), the sole source of truth for its fields (including `localized`/`required`/`validations`)
+3. Run `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` for each environment in the promotion chain
+**To run it:**
+npm run install:contentful -- --target dev
+Requires `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (scope:shared) and `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account (scope:personal, never pushed to the centrally-shared GitHub Environments store, but fine to hold locally). Both live in your local, gitignored `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold them, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running). Get the management token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.
+Both scripts are idempotent — safe to re-run. Field deletion during an install is opt-in
+(`--delete-deleted-fields` on `install:contentful`), off by default.
+**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding content-type entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

content.content:
═══════════ af87b5b
docs(fonts): reconcile six font statements that contradicted the code

Futura Round has been self-hosted since 34486eb, but six places still described the opposite
or claimed a restriction nothing implements. A reader following any of them would reach the
wrong conclusion, and one was actively steering designers away from the review the fonts were
added to enable.

- .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md said "self-hosted for development and testing". There is no
  environment gate: ZimmFontFace mounts unconditionally inside _app-config's ChakraProvider,
  and pwa-kit-dev's staticFolderCopyPlugin copies overrides/app/static in both the client and
  SSR webpack configs, so the .woff2 publish with every bundle. Now says so explicitly,
  because the previous wording implied a gate that does not exist.
- overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts asserted the inverse of reality — "not self-hosted,
  the Monotype licence forbids it, so the fallback is what customers actually render".
- overrides/app/components/foundation/typography.stories.tsx told designers not to sign off
  brand type there because specimens render the fallback. .storybook/preview.tsx mounts
  ZimmFontFace, so they render the real face. Inverted, with a note that a ~13%-wide specimen
  means the face failed to load.
- theme/components/footer.ts's "(unlicensed for web)" parenthetical dropped; the fallback-vs-
  Futura width measurements it annotated are still correct and still needed, because the column
  cap has to hold before the self-hosted face loads as well as after.
- .docs/architecture.md and .docs/memory/projectState.md corrected.

The Monotype Web Page Content entitlement is recorded in frozenFiles.md as an open item with
the licence path, rather than dropped. An earlier revision deleted that clause, and the
pre-commit AI-rules sync propagated the deletion into .cursor/rules/ and
.github/copilot-instructions.md — removing the only in-repo record of the constraint.

Tier 1 files touched, both text-only: .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md (Governance) and
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts (Design System, UI Designer owned). Proceeding under
the verified-session exception in AGENTS.md — authenticated as marcelannavarro, a member of
@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers. No token, stack, or font value changed in either.

═══════════ a728bea
docs(header): drop an unsupported HPC-025 citation from the icon-block comments

Both comments claimed "Account is present as text, so nothing is missing" about
HPC-018's confirmed Search / Account / Bag header set. That is true at `lg`+ and
false below it, where the mobile cluster renders Search / Store Locator / Bag.

The first attempt at rescoping them cited HPC-025 as confirming the mobile
arrangement was deliberate. That citation is wrong. HPC-025 appears twice in
.docs/prd/homepage.md and both concern the country/region selector — it confirms
mobile navigation is a hamburger menu and that the selector sits inside it. It
says nothing about Account, and no requirement states that mobile chrome
generally surfaces controls in the drawer. The claim generalised from a single
placement note about a different control.

What the comments now say instead, all verifiable: Account is text-only at `lg`+;
below `lg` it is absent from the header but still reachable via base drawer-menu
("My Account", "Sign In"); no PRD confirms the drawer as HPC-018's intended
satisfaction, so that is an open question rather than compliance; and there are
two discrepancies against HPC-018 below `lg`, not one — Account is missing where
the requirement names it, and Store Locator is present although homepage.md:19
says "Locate Boutique ... not part of the header".

Comment-only; no functional or visual change. The wrong citation had also been
posted in a PR review reply, which has been corrected in-thread rather than
silently amended here.

overrides/app/components/header/ is Squad A territory and Tier 2 shared shell
(.claude/rules/squadA.md, protectedFiles.md) — Squad B notification is owed even
for a comment change.

═══════════ 542ac65
docs(rules): align governance docs with this branch's footer/uiCopy patterns

Reviewed .claude/rules/ and .claude/skills/ against what this branch actually
established over the footer-CDA-wiring and useUiCopy-globalization work.
Found and fixed concrete gaps, not just drift:

- components.md: the container/presentational rule blocked leaf components
  from calling data-fetching hooks with no exception, but we deliberately had
  BottomBar/ZimmSubscribeSection call useUiCopy() directly — app-wide static
  content read from a Provider mounted once at the root (same pattern as
  useIntl), not a per-page fetch. Documented the exception so the next
  session doesn't either avoid a legitimate pattern or misapply it to a real
  SDK hook.
- testing.md: "don't duplicate coverage across layers" had no guidance on
  *how* to resolve that tension, which is exactly what led to two rounds of
  user correction on ZimmSubscribeSection's test suite. Clarified: scope the
  assertions (mock what's covered elsewhere), don't skip the component's own
  file. Also documented the ZimmIcon/Vitest SVG-barrel gap discovered this
  branch (no test had ever rendered an icon-consuming component before).
- protectedFiles.md + CODEOWNERS: uiCopyProvider/ is mounted at the app root
  in _app-config (same blast radius as _app-config itself) but had no
  CODEOWNERS entry at all — no required review routing, unlike every other
  Global Shell path. Added it to both.
- new-component/SKILL.md, code-quality/SKILL.md: same two fixes as
  components.md/testing.md, applied to the scaffolding flow and the
  audit checklist (Agent D no longer treats a play function in an unrelated
  component's story as a substitute for this component's own test file).

Edited under verified tier-1-approvers identity (gh api user + team
membership check) per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval process.

═══════════ e686bd3
test(theme): make the recipe guards fail on empty input and see responsive forms

Three changes, the first of which is the reason for the other two.

All four existing guards assert `expect(offenders).toEqual([])`, and an empty input satisfies
that exactly as well as a clean one. Stubbing the components map to {} left every test green —
verified — so four regression guards written from four shipped defects could have stopped
checking silently. A collect()-is-non-empty precondition fixes that. A `> 0` floor rather than
pinned counts: during this work a sibling change registered a recipe and the measurement moved
441 entries / 6 recipes to 453 / 7, so a pinned number would already be red.

walk() reported the leaf key as `prop`, making responsive forms invisible: `width: 'xl'` and
`_hover: {boxSize: '2xs'}` were caught, `width: ['xl','2xl']` and `width: {base:'xl'}` were not
— which are exactly the shapes overrideStyling.md teaches. Carrying the last key forward fixes
only the array case, because `base`/`md` are not numeric indices; detecting a responsive
*container* handles both. The all-keys-are-breakpoints test is load-bearing: `xl` and `2xl` are
keys in breakpoints *and* spacing, so a per-key check would misread Chakra's own
`sizes: {md, lg}` recipe shape as responsive. 18 cases, 10 of them deliberate false-positive
controls, zero misfires. It also reattributes 6 real leaves in header.ts's logoBar, a
3-element responsive array every prop-keyed guard was structurally blind to.

The sizing trap has an undocumented twin on typography: fontSizes, lineHeights and
letterSpacings are never registered, so `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was
intended, and `'4xs'` emits nothing at all. Guarded alongside the sizing props. fontWeight is
deliberately excluded — `medium` is a key in both scales and resolves to 500 either way, so the
same rule would flag a correct declaration.

Scope limit worth stating: this walks the recipe map only, so it cannot see JSX props. There is
a live instance outside its reach — header/index.tsx's `fontSize="l"` emits nothing, since `l`
is a space key and not a fontSizes key. Pre-existing on develop, not fixed here; catching that
class needs an ast-grep rule over JSX attributes, which .coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/ is the
right home for.

Whole file measures 2ms.

═══════════ ec9d161
fix(registry): make union prop resolution order-independent and fail closed

Two defects in 13add6e's union handling, both reproduced before fixing.

Partial unions were published as complete. `.filter(Boolean)` dropped members
declared in other files and the bail-out only fired when every member failed,
so `A | B` with an external B resolved to A's props alone — and with
members.length shrunk to 1, every surviving prop satisfied the
present-in-every-member test and was reported required. Now all-or-nothing:
if any member is unresolvable the union expression is returned.

Requiredness depended on declaration order. Optionality was inferred from
presence count and the first member's text was kept verbatim, so a prop that
one variant makes optional could be published as mandatory. Reversing
ZimmButton's operands turned `variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'` into
`variant: 'icon'` — the same false-requiredness claim 13add6e set out to fix,
relocated. A prop is now required only where every member carries it and every
member declares it without `?`, and types are unioned across members instead
of taken from whichever operand came first.

Within a member an intersection may declare a prop twice (the base's
`label: string` plus the member's own literal); `A & B` must satisfy both, so
the member requires the prop if any declaration does.

ZimmButton is the only affected row: variant and size now show their full
unions, `label` stays required, and the `?` markers are stable under operand
reversal. Generator remains idempotent.

═══════════ e686bd3
test(theme): make the recipe guards fail on empty input and see responsive forms

Three changes, the first of which is the reason for the other two.

All four existing guards assert `expect(offenders).toEqual([])`, and an empty input satisfies
that exactly as well as a clean one. Stubbing the components map to {} left every test green —
verified — so four regression guards written from four shipped defects could have stopped
checking silently. A collect()-is-non-empty precondition fixes that. A `> 0` floor rather than
pinned counts: during this work a sibling change registered a recipe and the measurement moved
441 entries / 6 recipes to 453 / 7, so a pinned number would already be red.

walk() reported the leaf key as `prop`, making responsive forms invisible: `width: 'xl'` and
`_hover: {boxSize: '2xs'}` were caught, `width: ['xl','2xl']` and `width: {base:'xl'}` were not
— which are exactly the shapes overrideStyling.md teaches. Carrying the last key forward fixes
only the array case, because `base`/`md` are not numeric indices; detecting a responsive
*container* handles both. The all-keys-are-breakpoints test is load-bearing: `xl` and `2xl` are
keys in breakpoints *and* spacing, so a per-key check would misread Chakra's own
`sizes: {md, lg}` recipe shape as responsive. 18 cases, 10 of them deliberate false-positive
controls, zero misfires. It also reattributes 6 real leaves in header.ts's logoBar, a
3-element responsive array every prop-keyed guard was structurally blind to.

The sizing trap has an undocumented twin on typography: fontSizes, lineHeights and
letterSpacings are never registered, so `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was
intended, and `'4xs'` emits nothing at all. Guarded alongside the sizing props. fontWeight is
deliberately excluded — `medium` is a key in both scales and resolves to 500 either way, so the
same rule would flag a correct declaration.

Scope limit worth stating: this walks the recipe map only, so it cannot see JSX props. There is
a live instance outside its reach — header/index.tsx's `fontSize="l"` emits nothing, since `l`
is a space key and not a fontSizes key. Pre-existing on develop, not fixed here; catching that
class needs an ast-grep rule over JSX attributes, which .coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/ is the
right home for.

Whole file measures 2ms.

═══════════ ec9d161
fix(registry): make union prop resolution order-independent and fail closed

Two defects in 13add6e's union handling, both reproduced before fixing.

Partial unions were published as complete. `.filter(Boolean)` dropped members
declared in other files and the bail-out only fired when every member failed,
so `A | B` with an external B resolved to A's props alone — and with
members.length shrunk to 1, every surviving prop satisfied the
present-in-every-member test and was reported required. Now all-or-nothing:
if any member is unresolvable the union expression is returned.

Requiredness depended on declaration order. Optionality was inferred from
presence count and the first member's text was kept verbatim, so a prop that
one variant makes optional could be published as mandatory. Reversing
ZimmButton's operands turned `variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'` into
`variant: 'icon'` — the same false-requiredness claim 13add6e set out to fix,
relocated. A prop is now required only where every member carries it and every
member declares it without `?`, and types are unioned across members instead
of taken from whichever operand came first.

Within a member an intersection may declare a prop twice (the base's
`label: string` plus the member's own literal); `A & B` must satisfy both, so
the member requires the prop if any declaration does.

ZimmButton is the only affected row: variant and size now show their full
unions, `label` stays required, and the `?` markers are stable under operand
reversal. Generator remains idempotent.
