content.content:
refactor(zimm-text-input): move colour derivation from the hook into the theme recipe

useZimmTextInputState was deriving border and label colours itself, which put
Figma's colour cascade in a hook while every other visual decision for the
component lived in its recipe. resolveBorderColour, resolveHoverBorderColour and
resolveLabelColour now live in theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts, and the hook
returns only interaction state (focused, filled, hasError).

The recipe is the single styling surface for the component, so a variant or
state added later cannot disagree with the hook about what colour applies.

═══════
feat(footer): wire footer container to live Contentful footerConfig content

FooterContainer now fetches footerConfig via the Delivery API (client.getEntries,
include: 3) instead of a hardcoded fixture, resolving the right entry for the
current storefront's region via resolveByRegion's pickMostSpecificByRegion/
filterByRegion utilities. Renders nothing on load/error/no-match rather than
falling back to placeholder content.

Also:
- fix(utils): widen resolveByRegion's RegionAwareEntry.sys type past a TS "weak
  type" false positive — this was its first real consumer against concrete
  entry types, exposing a latent bug that blocked every content-type generic
  from satisfying the constraint.
- rename contentfulFixture.ts -> index.stories.content.ts, since it now only
  ever feeds index.stories.tsx (Storybook), not the live container.
- chore(contentful): bootstrapSpace.mjs now creates non-default locales as
  optional: true, so a required localized field can publish with only 'en'
  set — translation happens later via a separate app, not as a publish
  precondition.

content.content:
═══════════ 1ed34ea
fix(security): close the backslash and control-character bypasses in isSafeHref

`e9c2180` closed `//host` and the docblock claimed the class was handled. It was not. Three
more forms resolved off-site:

    isSafeHref('/\example.com')   -> true, resolves to https://example.com/
    isSafeHref('/\/evil.com')     -> true, resolves to https://evil.com/
    isSafeHref('/<TAB>/evil.com') -> true, resolves to https://evil.com/

Two distinct causes.

A browser treats `/\host` as `//host`, so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as
a second slash is. The lookahead only excluded the forward slash — now `(?![/\\])`.

The WHATWG URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere in
the input *before* it parses, so `/<TAB>/evil.com` is parsed as `//evil.com`. The guard was
testing the raw string while the browser resolved a different one. Fixed by normalising the same
way the parser does, then testing. A plain space is deliberately not stripped — the parser
percent-encodes it, so `/ /evil.com` stays on-site and must remain allowed. That case is in the
tests precisely so this is not read as "reject anything unusual".

Why the existing tests did not catch it: all 13 were derived from the same mental model as the
regex, and not one contained a backslash or a control character. The util was extracted in
f664f59 and reported as covered on that basis. Seven cases added — six rejections and the space
allowance — and mutation-tested orthogonally: restoring the old lookahead fails exactly the two
backslash cases, removing the normalise step fails exactly the three control-character cases.

`no-control-regex` is suppressed at the two regex declarations with the reason inline. The rule
exists to catch control characters appearing by accident; here they are the subject.

Latent rather than live today — every href the guard sees comes from FOOTER_FIXTURE, a
developer-authored constant. It goes hot when HPC-034 swaps in the Contentful fetch and editor
═══════════ 52b8ac1
refactor(ui-kit): drop a cast justified by a false claim, and freeze the CMS arrays

ZimmIcon carried two `as` casts under the comment "TypeScript cannot index a discriminated
union type directly — each branch must be cast individually". That is not true: both keys exist
in every member of the union (one required, one optional-never), so the rest object indexes
directly. Deleting the casts compiles clean. They also widened 'aria-hidden' from
`true | undefined` to `boolean | undefined`, losing literal precision for nothing.

Being precise about severity, since an earlier reading of mine overstated it: the casts did NOT
weaken the XOR. That is enforced by the parameter annotation, which a body-local cast cannot
reach — all four invalid call sites are still rejected with the casts present, verified. So this
was a false explanatory comment plus needless imprecision, not a safety hole. The comment is
replaced rather than deleted, because "add a cast here" is exactly what a future reader would
reintroduce.

FooterNavGroupEntry.links, FooterConfigEntry.navGroups and .legalLinks are now readonly
ReadonlyArray. The footer only maps over them — an exhaustive search for mutation methods
across overrides/ found none — but FOOTER_FIXTURE is a module-level singleton consumed by the
production container, and a probe doing push/index-assign/sort/length=0 compiled before this.
Both modifiers pull weight: ReadonlyArray blocks the array operations, the property modifier
blocks whole-array reassignment. Applied to a full isolated copy of overrides/ it compiles at
exit 0 with nothing breaking, while rejecting all seven mutation vectors. It also aligns the
entry types with BottomBarProps.legalLinks, which already used ReadonlyArray in the same file.

Both are type-level and erased at build.

═══════════ 2c4ab7a
refactor(footer): replace type assertions with honest signatures on the guard path

Four uncommented `as` casts, all on branches that matter.

isSafeHref returns a plain boolean, which carries no narrowing, so the contact row had to
re-assert `href as string` inside the branch the guard had already proved — on the line that
decides `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, the attribute that stops the storefront URL reaching
WhatsApp in the Referer header. A `href is string` predicate was tried and rejected as
unsound: `javascript:void(0)` is a string that returns false, so the else branch would
narrow to `undefined`. Widening leavesTheSite makes no narrowing claim at all and leaves
safeHref's shared contract untouched.

ZimmNavItem's two `as React.MouseEventHandler<...>` casts were never needed — parameter
contravariance already allows a union-typed handler where an element-specific one is
expected; verified by deleting them. They were live suppressions on the prop's only wiring
point: narrowing ZimmNavItemProps.onClick to one element would no longer fail to compile.

namedItem keeps `| null` rather than asserting it away, so the `?.` that follows has
something real to catch. Mirrors zimmInputAction's handleSubmit.

+  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
+  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
+  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
+  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
+  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
+  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
+- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
+  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.
+   - No data-fetching hooks of any kind (commerce SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or React Query) — accept data as props; the parent (a page or container component) owns data fetching. See components.md → Composition → Container/presentational separation. Exception: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called directly — they read from a Provider mounted once at the app root and degrade gracefully with none present, so they don't create the reuse problem this rule exists to prevent. See components.md's exception note for the full reasoning.
+4. If the component owns non-trivial logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping decisions, event wiring), create `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx` (Vitest) in the same folder — even if that logic's effects are also covered by a hook's own test or a parent's assembly-level Storybook `play`. Resolve any duplication by mocking the hook/child whose internals are proven elsewhere and testing only this component's own contract, not by skipping the file. See testing.md's note under "What to test (and what to skip)". Skip only when the component has no branching/decision logic at all (pure prop interpolation).

content.text:
# SFCC-55 Global Footer (PR #59) — Engineering Playbook Extract

Read-only analysis. Nothing was modified, committed, or pushed.

---

## 1. Commit range

**Merge commit:** `8362b3cfbacafdb3d37f106e1c77eff53f5f9cbc` — *"Merge pull request #59 from ZimmermannAU/feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui"*, Mon 24 Aug 2026, author `marcelannavarro`.

**Range settled on:** `8362b3c^1..8362b3c^2` → `cd68e97..604ece5` = **93 commits**, `8c25f11` (first) … `604ece5` (last).

**How determined, and why this range is exact:**
- `git rev-parse 8362b3c^1 8362b3c^2` gives `cd68e97` (develop tip before merge) and `604ece5` (branch tip). The `^1..^2` form yields precisely what the second parent adds over the first.
- Cross-checked against `gh pr view 59 --json commits --jq '.commits|length'` → **93**, same head and tail commits. Two independent sources agree.
- `git log --merges 8362b3c^1..8362b3c^2` is **empty** — the branch was rebased, never had `develop` merged into it. That matters: with no inner merges, the range contains only PR content, no incidentally-swept commits.
- Authors: Marcel Angelo Navarro 54, Jersey Perez 25, TimLavelle 14 — consistent with the PR body's disclosure that *"this branch was taken over from Jersey."*

Commit-type shape (useful signal on its own): 12 `fix(footer)`, 9 `refactor(footer)`, 8 `feat(footer)`, 7 `fix(ui-kit)`, 6 `refactor(ui-kit)`, 5 `fix(registry)`, plus **10 `docs(...)` commits whose entire purpose was correcting project docs that the code had diverged from**. That last cluster is a pattern in its own right (see §6).

---

## 2. What was actually built

### `overrides/app/components/footer/`

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.tsx` | Two exports: `Footer` (presentational, `data` **required**, fetches nothing) and default `FooterContainer` (the only place the Contentful fetch lives). Also exports `scopeToRegion`. ~219 lines. |
| `footer.css.ts` | `ZimmFooter` recipe — shell only: `container`, `main`, `contentRow`, `subscribe`, `links`, `linksInner`, `logo`, `logoButton`. |
| `footerNavColumn/index.tsx` | One nav column: heading, link list, optional contact-icon row. Exports testable `hasIntentionalLineBreak`. |
| `footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts` | `ZimmFooterNavColumn` — `col`, `heading`, `list`, `listItem`. |
| `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` | Vitest — 3 pure-fn cases + 4 render-branch cases. |
| `bottomBar/index.tsx` | Locale placeholder, copyright, legal links. Calls `useUiCopy()` directly. |
| `bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` | `ZimmFooterBottomBar` — 8 parts. |
| `index.stories.tsx` | `Layout/Footer`, 5 stories, 4 with `play`. |
| `index.stories.content.ts` | `FOOTER_FIXTURE` — Storybook-only, shaped as a resolved CDA response. |
| `index.test.tsx` | Vitest — `scopeToRegion` pure logic (5) + `FooterContainer` fetch/resolve integration (7). |

**No `.scss` anywhere in the footer or `ui-kits`.** Every visual decision is a Chakra recipe. That is the norm this PR set.

### ui-kits it depends on

```
atoms/     zimmLogo · zimmIcon · zimmNavItem · zimmButton · zimmTextInput · zimmModal
molecules/ zimmContactIconRow · zimmInputAction
organisms/ zimmSubscribeSection · zimmSubscribeModal
```

**The atoms/molecules/organisms rule, read off the actual imports** (this is *not* "how many DOM nodes"):
- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop + `role="dialog"` chrome, because **it owns no content** (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all come from the caller).
- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button + local validation state.
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection` owns the subscribe state machine (via `useSubscribeSection`) and the HPC-035 modal decision.

**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) → `Forms/`; `zimmContactIconRow` (molecule) → `Elements/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Folder = composition depth; `title` = domain. Don't conflate them.

### Recipe wiring

`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:1-35` imports recipes **from the component folders** and re-exports one flat map:

```ts
import { ZimmFooter } from 'app/components/footer/footer.css';
import { ZimmFooterNavColumn } from 'app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css';
import { ZimmModal } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/zimmModal.css';
```

Only `header.ts` and `listMenu.ts` still live in `theme/components/` as registered recipes. `footerShared.ts` stays there deliberately (cross-file values, not one component's).

Consumption is always the same three lines — a recipe key as a module constant, then `useMultiStyleConfig`:

```ts
// footer/index.tsx:15, :88
const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE, {});
```

---

## 3. Established patterns to copy

### 3.1 Co-located `<name>.css.ts` — and the governance twist

`overrideStyling.md` now says a recipe may live beside its component. **The non-obvious part is that this changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS` gained, deliberately placed *last* among the `components/` rules:

```
# CODEOWNERS uses last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins
overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts   @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b
```

So a `.css.ts` inside `footer/` (Tier 2 Global Shell) drops the Tier 1/2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries, while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. Rationale: a co-located recipe *composes established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).

**The repo flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it** — `overrideStyling.md` carries a blockquote noting that `zimmButton.css.ts`'s unapproved provisional constants are now squad-gated while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe, and calls it "an open governance question, not a doc fix."

**Copy this:** recipe beside component, key registered in `theme/components/index.ts`, key as a named module constant. Chakra resolves by string key, not path — the move is zero-runtime-risk.

### 3.2 `var(--zimm-*)` over bare Chakra keys — mechanically enforced

Hierarchy: `textStyle` for type → `var(--zimm-*)` for colour/spacing → recipe → `sx` → `.scss` (never reached in this PR).

The rule changed *during* this PR (`9d5f89c`) from "preferred" to **required**, and the same commit built the guard that enforces it. From the commit body:

> "bare Chakra token keys and `var(--zimm-*)` both resolve correctly today, but a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it's actually correct."

`recipeGuards.test.ts` (365 lines, runs on `npm run test`) has **five** guards, four of which encode a real shipped defect:

1. **spacing key on a sizing prop** — `width: 'xl'` reads `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem, not `space.xl`. *"It shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer."*
2. **spacing/scale key on a typography prop** — `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are **not registered**. `fontSize: '2xs'` → Chakra's 10px where 14px was meant; `fontSize: 'l'` → declaration dropped entirely.
3. **recipe name colliding with a base SFCC recipe** — `extendTheme` *deep merges*. `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']`; everything else must be namespaced (`ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`).
4. **bare key inside a compound shorthand** — `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim; browser drops it.
5. **house style** — the bare-vs-`var()` rule.

Three sub-lessons in that test file that transfer to *any* guard you write:

- **`test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`** exists because every other guard asserts `toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies. Stubbing `components` to `{}` turned the whole file green — verified.
- The guard resolves a function-form `baseStyle` across **all 2^5 = 32 boolean prop combinations**, not one default. The original bug (`top: floated ? '3xs' : '50%'`) hid down a conditional branch the single-resolution walk never entered.
- It knows its own blind spot and says so: `SCOPE:` note names a **live, unfixed instance at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311`** (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) that a theme walk structurally cannot reach.

Complementary, broader, and **not in CI**: `npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) greps for raw hex/px/rem/em. Its acknowledged-exception mechanism is smart — it reads the *existing* comment block (`provisional` / `pending` / `placeholder` / `audit-allow:`) rather than maintaining a second allow-list that would drift. First run surfaced 14 pre-existing violations, which is exactly why it isn't a gate yet.

### 3.3 Responsive steps = explicit media queries, never array shorthand

```ts
// footer.css.ts:43-48
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: {
  flexDirection: 'row',
  padding: `var(--zimm-scale-4xl) var(--zimm-scale-3xl) ${SPACE_SECTION}`,
},
```

Two reasons, both non-obvious: the array form (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) puts a bare token key at every step and the guard flags all four; and `BP.desktop` (64em) **conflicts with Chakra's `lg`=62em / `xl`=80em**, so a responsive prop would silently step at the wrong width.

`footerShared.ts` holds the two genuinely cross-file values, imports `breakpoints.md` rather than retyping it, and carries an explicit `audit-allow:` for its `em` literals — *"raw em is correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token."*

### 3.4 Container / presentational split

`Footer` takes `data: FooterConfigEntry` as a **required** prop. From its JSDoc (`footer/index.tsx:63-66`):

> "`data` is required by design: static content belongs in the story or in the container below, never baked into the component that renders production UI."

`FooterContainer` is the default export because **base SFCC `_app` renders `<Footer />` with no props** — so there is no upstream container and the wrapper *is* the seam (`index.tsx:159-162`).

The code self-flags its own rule tension rather than hiding it (`index.tsx:169-170`):

> "Note this puts a fetch inside `components/`, which components.md reserves for containers; if that matters, this should move into an `_app` override instead (Tier 2 shared shell — coordinate first)."

**Two upstream gotchas the container encodes:**

- `useMultiSite()` ships untyped; it's cast inline with the reasoning recorded, cross-referenced against `useCountryConfig.ts` as precedent.
- `buildUrl` + `history.push`, **not** `useNavigation` (`index.tsx:173-177`) — `useNavigation` special-cases `path === '/'` and drops the site/locale prefix, dumping a prefixed-storefront shopper onto the default site.

### 3.5 Region scoping — `overrides/app/utils/resolveByRegion.ts`

Two functions, deliberately different semantics:

- **`filterByRegion`** — inclusive. Use where multiple regional entries can coexist in one rendered list (links inside a shared nav group).
- **`pickMostSpecificByRegion`** — single winner. Use for a root entry.

Model: **omitted/empty `regions` = global = *least* specific**; fewer regions = more specific (`specificity()` returns `Infinity` for unscoped). Contentful applies no region scoping of its own, so `scopeToRegion` re-maps the whole tree after resolution.

The tie-break is the transferable part (`resolveByRegion.ts:71-91`). Commit `7e8f3cc`:

> "the warn and the reassignment both sat inside `if (candidateUpdatedAt > bestUpdatedAt)`. Equal or absent timestamps failed the strict `>`, so nothing fired and whichever entry the CDA happened to return first won. **`getEntries` is called with no `order`, so that is not stable across requests.**"

Fix: warn hoisted **outside** the comparison (the tie is the editorial defect worth surfacing, regardless of who wins), `sys.id` as deterministic secondary key. And the meta-lesson:

> "The suite was testing around the bug. `test('order of the tied candidates in the input does not change the outcome')` used only *distinct* timestamps — the one arrangement that was already order-independent."

The type is worth copying too — `RegionAwareEntry.sys` carries a deliberate index signature to escape TypeScript's "weak type" check, with the reason inline (`resolveByRegion.ts:15-18`).

Content model (`scripts/contentful/content-types/region.js`): `region` is a **first-class referenceable entity** with a `siteId` join key (`validations: [{unique: true}]`) matching SFCC site IDs — not a hardcoded site-ID list duplicated per content type.

### 3.6 Absent / failed CMS data — a deliberate three-tier policy

This is the single most reusable decision in the PR. **The policy differs by what the content *is*:**

| Content class | Behaviour | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | Render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | `footer/index.tsx:214` | *"no fallback to placeholder content once wired to live data, so a Contentful outage doesn't silently ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers"* |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | Fall back to the **English literal** | `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:33` | *"unlike structural content … losing a button label or a status message to a Contentful outage should never blank a control"* |
| **Per-item destination** (contact href) | Degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:86-88` | Perceivable but not a false affordance |

The per-item case is the most carefully argued (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:76-85`):

> "NON-INTERACTIVE but PERCEIVABLE: `<span>`: no href, no tabIndex, so nothing promises an action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4). labelled, not aria-hidden: ZimmIcon emits `role="img"` + `aria-label`, so screen reader users learn the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoids the 1.1.1 information loss the previous aria-hidden caused)."

**Same treatment reused three times** for "control with no action": the contact fallback, `ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders `<button>`, no scroll/redirect), and `BottomBar`'s locale placeholder (a `<div>`, not a `<button>`).

**Also copy:** never branch on localised CMS text. `footerNavGroup` gained a `showContactChannels: boolean` field, with the reason in the type (`types/contentful.ts:113-116`):

> "A flag rather than matching the heading text: `heading` is a localised Contentful value, so `heading === 'Contact'` silently stops matching the moment an editor writes 'Kontakt' or 'Contacto' — and this footer ships to eight storefronts."

**Security gate:** every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. `include: 3` is load-bearing, not arbitrary (`footer/index.tsx:17-27`) — at depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs, `region.fields.siteId` throws, `.catch` swallows it, and **the entire footer renders nothing**.

### 3.7 `useUiCopy` — Context, not a fetch

`useUiCopy.ts:38` is one line:

```ts
export const useUiCopy = (): UiCopyContextValue => useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
```

`UiCopyProvider` bulk-fetches every `uiCopy` entry in **one** CDA call, mounted once at `_app-config/index.tsx:161`. Call sites read `t('footer.copyright.label', 'Copyright')` — key plus English fallback, both at the call site.

**This is now a documented exception to container/presentational** (`components.md`, added by `542ac65`): Context-backed app-wide static-content hooks may be called from presentational leaves. The narrowness matters — *"content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, not anything that varies per page."*

**The no-Provider behaviour difference is the sharp edge, and the docs got it wrong first.** `useUiCopy` degrades silently. **`useIntl` throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by **base SFCC `_app`**, not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it. The rule doc explicitly retracts its own earlier claim: *"An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed both hooks degrade gracefully and that both Providers sit in `_app-config`; neither is true of `useIntl`."*

Design arc worth knowing (`90069b2`): this started as footer-container-fetch-and-prop-drill, which *"only worked because FooterContainer was the sole consumer."* Context removed the redundant-fetch concern that motivated prop-drilling in the first place, and every threaded label prop was deleted.

`uiCopyProvider/` was added to **Tier 2** and CODEOWNERS in the same PR — *"same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, so it belongs in this tier rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission."*

### 3.8 Test layering — what got which layer, and the stated reasoning

**13 Vitest files added.** Pure logic and integration boundaries: `resolveByRegion`, `safeHref`, `useSubscribeSection`, `useZimmModal`, `useZimmTextInputState`, `useUiCopy`, `uiCopyProvider`, `fontFace`, `recipeGuards`, `zimmTextInput.css`, plus three component files.

**15 story files with `play`.** Real-browser behaviour: focus traps, scroll lock, layout-shift measurement, `rel`/`target` attributes.

The split rule, verbatim from `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx:18-22`:

> "The real modal's focus-trap/portal mechanics are already covered by `useZimmModal.test.tsx` (synthetic harness) and `footer/index.stories.tsx`'s `SubscribeModalOpen` play (mutation-tested, real browser). Stubbing it here keeps this suite scoped to ZimmSubscribeSection's own contract — does it wire the right props into its children — rather than a second copy of coverage that already exists elsewhere."

That file mocks **three** things (`useSubscribeSection`, `ZimmSubscribeModal`, `useUiCopy`), each with a comment naming where the real coverage lives. **`testing.md` was amended by this PR to make that the rule**: resolve duplication by *scoping what the file asserts*, not by skipping the component's own test file — because *"relying on a different component's story to prove this component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder."* `BottomBar` (pure prop interpolation, no branching) correctly has no suite.

**Four practices that would be non-obvious to copy:**

1. **A recipe file can export pure resolvers and unit-test them.** `zimmTextInput.css.ts` exports `resolveBorderColour` / `resolveHoverBorderColour` / `resolveLabelColour`; `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` asserts the precedence cascade directly instead of on generated CSS. Colour derivation was deliberately moved *out of the hook into the recipe* (`3220239`) so *"a variant or state added later cannot disagree with the hook about what colour applies."*

2. **Anchor before/after assertions above zero or they pass vacuously.** `index.stories.tsx:231-237`:
   > "The two equality checks below are pure before/after comparisons, so a collapsed container satisfies them vacuously: `display:none`, `height:0;overflow:hidden` and an ancestor `display:none` each measure 0 both times and pass. Every rect is 0 in jsdom too."
   Plus `LAYOUT_PRECISION_DP = 1` — `getBoundingClientRect` sub-pixel jitter would fail an exact equality on a layout that didn't move.

3. **Mutation testing is the evidence standard, repeatedly.** Recurring phrasing across commits: *"Mutation-tested rather than assumed"*; *"reintroducing the bare '3xs' and confirming the guard fails on it"*; *"Un-hoisting the warn now fails 4 tests (1 before these additions)"*; *"defaulting the prop back to true fails it."*

4. **Known harness gap, now documented in `testing.md`:** `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest — it imports the base SFCC icons barrel whose top-level `AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...` fails because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings. Unfixable from a test file (`vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1). Two mock variants are the sanctioned workaround:
   ```ts
   vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))
   ```
   …or forward `aria-label`/`aria-hidden` when the assertion depends on the accessible name `ZimmIcon` itself carries (`footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx:14-21`).

## 4. Declined CodeRabbit findings → the rules they establish

58 actionable comments, 9 review rounds, 57 inline threads. The declines encode more project convention than the fixes do.

### Tier 1 / governance

**Only four paths are true absolutes.** CodeRabbit twice demanded reverting `.storybook/main.js` + `preview.tsx` citing Hard Rule #8. Declined, and CodeRabbit withdrew (*"My original finding incorrectly treated Hard Rule #8 as an absolute restriction"*). The argument:

> "Hard Rule #4 … names exactly four absolutes, and `.storybook/` is not among them. And it then takes another Tier 1 path — `.github/workflows/` … — and states the exception *does* apply to it. **So being Tier 1 is not by itself disqualifying; being one of the four named absolutes is.**"

→ **Rule:** the absolutes are `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. Everything else Tier 1 is reachable under the verified-session exception — run `gh api user`, check team membership, name the file and reason **in the commit body**.

**A comment-only fix to a frozen file beats relocating the correction.** On `theme/foundation/fonts.ts`:

> "**A false statement in a frozen file, at the point of use, is a worse outcome than a corrected one** — particularly for the next person deciding whether they are allowed to touch the fonts."

**But two concessions were volunteered, and they're the most useful part.** On `foundation/sizes.ts` (one comment line):

> "Our commit message argued 'Hard Rule #3's rationale isn't engaged' — **that is an over-read**; #3's operative text is an unconditional prohibition… the argument that actually holds is Hard Rule #4 plus the verified-session exception. And these two lines were **not necessary in this PR** — they could have been split into a separate designer-gated change at no cost. We're declining on precedent and mootness, not on necessity."

→ **Rule:** never argue "the rationale isn't engaged" against unconditional text. And an incidental Tier 1 comment fix that *could* be split out **should** be — declining on mootness is the weak position.

### Scope discipline (Hard Rule #5 / #10)

**`fontSize="l"` in `header/index.tsx:311` — confirmed real bug, declined anyway.** It dates to the repo's initial commit; this branch's only change to that file is 14 comment lines.

> "Correcting the token changes the rendered size of a header heading. That is a live visual change to Tier 2 shared shell … with no Figma review, inside a footer PR. **AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 covers this directly: fixing a bug in one component does not license touching its neighbours.**"

→ **Rules:** (a) systemic fix is an ast-grep JSX rule in `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` (Tier 1, needs its own story), not a one-off patch; (b) **never accept CodeRabbit's offer to open a GitHub issue** — this project tracks in Jira only, a GitHub issue is *"a parallel tracker nobody watches."*

**Cite the PRD line before you cite it.** The mobile-header decline originally cited HPC-025 as justification. It was publicly retracted in-thread:

> "**Correction to my reply above — I cited HPC-025 wrongly.** … it appears in exactly two places and both concern the **country/region selector** … **I generalised from a single placement note about a different control.** … **And your finding is stronger than I credited.**"

CodeRabbit's response — *"The earlier learning about HPC-025 is obsolete"* — is the point: a wrong citation in a decline **poisons CodeRabbit's learning store** and must be retracted in-thread, not silently amended in a later commit.

**A PR is not where you stand up a directory's first test harness.** Declined twice on this basis: `overrides/app/pages/` (zero tests since initial commit) and `scripts/` (no test file). *"Requiring the first one on this PR would turn a standing repo-wide gap into a gate on unrelated work."*

**A shared-hook signature change is an RFC, not a PR fix.** Adding `locale?` to `useContentfulEntries` was accepted as correct and declined: *"AGENTS.md's stop-and-ask table sends that to a team RFC, and Hard Rule #5 points the same way."*

### Conventions

**camelCase vs kebab-case is an *origin signal*, not style.** Demanded twice across 9 files, declined both times:

> "Every file named here is Zimmermann-authored with no base equivalent. Searching all 883 files of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` returns zero hits… Renaming would invert the rule's stated purpose — 'makes the origin of a file obvious at a glance' — **by falsely signalling Salesforce origin.**"

Root cause named as *ours*: stale boilerplate at `.cursor/rules/development-guidelines.mdc:96` that `syncCursorRules.mjs` doesn't emit. **Expect this finding to recur until that's reconciled.**

**Portal content is scoped to `document.body`, and that's not negotiable.** Demanded four times (`within(canvasElement)` per `testing.md:128`). Measured rebuttal:

> "`canvasElement.contains(dialog) === false`, 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the document, and `canvasElement.innerHTML` is 41 characters… the suggestion verbatim fails immediately with `getByRole`, and after a 1002ms timeout with `findByRole`, while the current body-scoped form passes in 1–2ms."

> "The alternative offered — a story-local portal target — would mean adding a portal-container prop to a shared atom purely to satisfy a test-scoping rule… **that's production API surface bought with no product value.**"

And the self-indictment: the in-code comments at `index.stories.tsx:77` and `:123` cite a **"testing.md §Layer-2 exception" that does not exist**. *"Until that lands this finding will keep re-firing, and that's a defect in our documentation rather than in your review."*

**"derived from", never "composed of"** — a LanguageTool suggestion rejected because it would trade an awkward-but-correct phrase for a fluent-but-wrong one. The house term for the token→class relationship is fixed.

**`site.id` is immutable for a mounted component's lifetime.** Declined "clear stale footer data before a replacement request":

> "`locals.site` is set only by `AppConfig.restore`, which the SDK calls in exactly two places… It never re-runs on a client-side route change… Every site/locale switch is a full document load."

→ Don't write defensive "site changed while mounted" resets.

**`*.stories.tsx` is out of scope for token/magic-number rules** — `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs:11-17` excludes it deliberately.

**`DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS` enumerates declared props only, never derived values.** `floated` is `Boolean(focused || filled)`; adding it would double 32→64 combinations for zero coverage plus a type-lie.

### ⚠️ One finding family produced *inconsistent* outcomes in the same PR

The `vi.clearAllMocks()` in `beforeEach` vs `afterEach` argument was **declined three times and accepted once**. The accepted one (`zimmTextInput.test.ts`, commit `a207b9a`) conceded:

> "**You're right that the rule in `.claude/rules/testing.md` is stated without qualification, and consistency with the convention as written is worth more than the argument.**"

Supporting evidence from the declines: `testing.md:67` dates to the repo's initial commit and *its own author* used `beforeEach(() => vi.clearAllMocks())` six days later; repo practice runs `beforeEach` 5 : `afterEach` 2.

→ **Rule:** when a repo rule is stated **unconditionally**, conform even for a provable no-op, and add an inline comment saying the hook resets nothing so the next reader doesn't hunt for phantom shared state (see `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:12-15` for that comment). A qualification to `testing.md:67` is proposed but **has not landed**.

## 6. Where the code contradicted or worked around the rules

**The most transferable meta-pattern in this PR: when code and a rule doc disagreed, the doc was fixed *in the same PR*, with the contradiction named.** Ten `docs(...)` commits did nothing else. `af87b5b` reconciled six font statements that asserted the opposite of what ships; `49a95b9` stopped `overrideStyling.md` instructing the bare token key its own new guard now fails the build on; `e00379c` corrected the `useIntl` claims; `ac224a6` fixed stale `button.ts` paths after co-location.

**Unresolved rule conflicts, surfaced but not fixed** (out of scope for a footer PR — Tier 1 governance needs both squad leads + Integration lead):

1. **Hard Rule #3/#8 are worded unconditionally, the Tier 1 Approval section grants an exception, and `frozenFiles.md` says "No exceptions."** This came up **three separate times** in one PR. The author's own read: *"the repetition is a signal that the docs are the defect."*
2. **`testing.md:128`** has no portal exception → the `within(canvasElement)` finding will keep re-firing.
3. **`testing.md:67`** (`clearAllMocks`) is unqualified, contradicts repo practice, and produced **inconsistent outcomes inside this PR**.
4. **`.cursor/rules/development-guidelines.mdc:96`** — stale kebab-case boilerplate contradicting the generated `conventions.mdc`.

**Documented rule tensions the footer code carries knowingly:**

- **Container/presentational** — `FooterContainer` fetches inside `components/`; self-flagged at `footer/index.tsx:169-170`.
- **`console.warn` in a shipped path** — `resolveByRegion.ts:77` fires on every editorial tie, ungated by `NODE_ENV`, and the JSDoc states it *"does reach shopper consoles."* `conventions.md` bans `console.log`/`console.error` and is silent on `console.warn` — a gap, not a granted exception.
- **`no-control-regex` suppressed inline** — `safeHref.ts:14-21`, with the reason at the point of use per the escape-hatch convention: *"The rule exists to catch control characters appearing by accident; here they are the subject."*
- **`theme/components/index.ts` imports from `app/components/**`** — inverted layering (theme depends on components). Not a cycle (`theme/components/index.ts` → `footer/footer.css.ts` → `theme/components/footerShared.ts` → `foundation/gridSystem`), but worth knowing before adding to it.
- **Import-style inconsistency** — every ui-kit uses the `app/components/ui-kits/...` alias except `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:3-5`, which uses `../../atoms/...`. Harmless (neither is an SFCC base path, so `overrideStyling.md`'s resolver trap doesn't apply) but inconsistent.

**Tier 1 files touched under the verified-session exception**, all disclosed in the PR body's Protection-tier block: `.storybook/main.js`, `.storybook/preview.tsx`, `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `theme/foundation/fonts.ts`, `theme/foundation/sizes.ts`. The two `foundation/` edits are **comment-only** (verified by diff — 1 line each, no token value changed). CodeRabbit flagged four and withdrew all four.

**A policy reversal shipped here:** fonts. `frozenFiles.md` previously said *"No font binaries in this repo"* on Monotype-licence grounds. This PR self-hosts two Futura Round faces with **no environment gate** — `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally in `_app-config`, and `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies `overrides/app/static` in both client and SSR webpack configs. The practical driver: *"the fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider,"* which had already caused wrong sizing decisions. Licence files are deliberately excluded from the repo; the Monotype entitlement is recorded as an open item.
